newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Monetary Authority opens office in New York.
newsitem.headline: HK Monetary Authority opens office in New York.

text.p: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) opened its first overseas office in New York, the government said in a statement on Friday.

The office will monitor foreign exchange and U.S. fixed income markets during the New York time zone and liaise with the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, other U.S. regulatory authorities and the HKMA Exchange Fund's external managers.
It will also monitor U.S. economic trends and represent the HKMA at official functions and events in the United States, including briefings on Hong Kong's monetary and banking systems.

"This office will enable us to ensure that our fingers are kept on the pulse of the market to facilitate the professional performance of our function as a full-fledged monetary authority," said HKMA chief executive Joseph Yam.

Hong Kong Financial Secretary Donald Tsang, who officiated the opening ceremony in New York on Thursday, New York time, said the office was one way to strengthen Hong Kong's links with other financial centres.
